purpose: High-compute corrected-group C5G7 transport study: confirm the canonical UMMU numerical reference screen and compare all six explicitly reformulated 2x2 UO2/MOX placement layouts under a common budget.

design.seed_policy: actual_seed = seed_base + stable design-space candidate-order offset; offsets are preserved in STUDY_SUMMARY.json

per_run_integrity: one completed statepoint per run; raw HDF5 audit passes
actual seed in settings equals run manifest and is unique across the 18 runs
shared MGXS SHA-256 and exact official C5G7 seven-group structure across all runs
settings exactly match the common profile
source entropy and k-generation traces preserved and reported, but not auto-certified solely by a scalar threshold
51x51 fission mesh present and assembly-integrated fission-rate proxy recomputed from statepoint

six_layout_comparison.purpose: descriptive high-budget comparison of the six reformulated layouts
six_layout_comparison.objective_status: not independently approved for final physical ranking
six_layout_comparison.rule: report all candidates, between-seed variation, within-run Monte Carlo uncertainty, and assembly fission-rate peaking proxy separately; do not label a winner physically optimal or safe

nonclaims: A passing numerical screen is not official OECD/NEA benchmark acceptance.
All six 2x2 layouts are not official independent C5G7 benchmark reference cases; only the canonical UMMU arrangement is used for the supplied scalar reference comparison.
This study is not reactor-safety certification.
The 2x2 UO2/MOX placement formulation is not a validated mapping of the legacy fresh/once-burned/twice-burned QUBO.
The assembly-integrated fission-rate peaking factor is a dimensionless proxy, not absolute power.
No physical superiority claim for CB-PFR is made before a predeclared, physically justified objective and independently reviewed reference tally comparison.

resources.note: Compute allocation estimate from configured batches times particles per batch; actual runtime and completion depend on hosted-runner throughput.
